text:
Ruth (CS): starting a short thread to draft an "edge" onboarding runbook for customers that are low-touch but high-risk for renewals. want a compact sheet customers can follow + an internal quick triage map.

Ben (SE): suggestion: make this runbook two-sided: customer copy (one pager) + internal play (ops checklist). include a tiny copyable JSON config so it looks different from the many YAML snippets.

Ruth (CS): good call. key customer-facing bullets i want: quick preflight, simple warmup, feedback cadence, and a tiny cost/latency snapshot customers can export for renewal conversations.

Kai (Product): renewal-watch signals (emphasize low-touch patterns):
- sudden drop in daily active sessions >25% over 48h (user engagement decline)
- repeated manual bypasses: customer disables caching/prefill more than twice in 7d (signals frustration)
- infra: cache_miss_rate spike >50% vs baseline in 6h OR sustained p95 latency > SLA + 400ms for 1h
Map these to an auto-tag "renewal_watch:edge" and notify CS.

Ben (SE): copyable JSON for quick customer paste into their onboarding config (they often use JS stacks):
```json
{
  "prefill": true,
  "prefill_ttl_seconds": 600,
  "batching": {
    "initial_batch_size": 3,
    "max_batch_size": 10,
    "jitter_ms": 20
  },
  "streaming": {
    "enabled": true,
    "partial_retry_limit": 1
  }
}
```

Ruth (CS): customer preflight checklist (one minute to skim):
- Run top-6 prompts (CS confirms success criteria)
- Enable prefill for bursty flows, TTL ~ 10min for session apps
- Start with conservative batching (init 3, max 10)
- Turn on streaming if you need progressive UX, else fall back to sync for stability
- Capture 3 sample prompts and attach to account notes

Kai (Product): add a tiny cost/latency snapshot template for renewals: 3 numbers customers like to see: median latency, p95 latency, avg token cost per 1k tokens. Example wording for slide: "After tuning: median 180ms (was 420ms), p95 420ms (was 950ms), estimated cost per 1k tokens down 14% via batching+cache." Keep it one line per metric.

Ben (SE): quick curl example to exercise prefill + streaming so customers can validate from their CI:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"prefill":true, "streaming":true, "prompts":["who are you?","summarize this: ..."]}'
```

Ruth (CS): feedback capture cadence tailored for low-touch customers: day0 (24h quick check), day7 (short 3-q form), day30 (optional deep feedback). Questions: latency ok? any workarounds you used? paste 3 high-priority prompts. store results in account notes automatically.

Kai (Product): observability sampling rules to include in docs: compute rolling baselines per customer for last 7d, then compare 24h windows. example rule: if cache_miss_rate > 150% of 7d baseline for 6h -> flag. prefer relative baselines for edge customers (they fluctuate).

Ben (SE): debugging tips we should hand the customer and internal SEs:
- run controlled test: set jitter_ms=0 for 10 minutes to reveal raw concurrency effects
- isolate batching: set initial_batch_size=1 and see if latency changes (helps isolate batching vs model cost)
- trace window: enable tracing for a tight 5-10 minute window and collect slow traces only

Ruth (CS): escalation steps (simple):
- If p95 > SLA + 400ms for 30m or cache_miss_rate spike persisted 2h -> CS opens priority ticket + SE pair within 1h
- If customer disables prefill twice or reports UX workarounds -> CS schedules 30-min customer check-in and marks renewal_watch:edge
- For streaming partial failures > 3x baseline in 6h -> immediate rollback to non-streaming route + SE investigation

Kai (Product): add a lightweight renewal score example for internal use:
- inputs: engagement_drop_48h (40%), cache_miss_ratio_change_24h (35%), customer_reported_workarounds (25%)
- quick rule: score > 0.55 => outreach. note: weights are adjustable.

Ben (SE): small note to SEs: avoid enabling model quantization for edge trials without a baseline A/B quality run. call out in doc: "Do not QAT mid-trial."

Ruth (CS): draft customer-facing one-liner to top the page: "Quick runbook: preflight, warm, validate, and share a 3-number snapshot for renewals. We’ll help interpret the snapshot." short and approachable.

HealthBot: template saved: "edge-onboard-runbook-compact" by Ruth.

Ruth (CS): action items before EOD:
- i'll author the 1-page customer PDF + a 2-line renewal snapshot template
- Ben: add the JSON snippet to the onboarding repo & give a copy link (24h)
- Kai: wire the renewal_watch:edge tag into console alerts (next sprint)

Ben (SE): noted. I'll drop the repo link when done.

Ruth (CS): thanks all 44d i'll post the draft here for a 10-min review.
